sections.text: Refunds are eligible when a billing error is confirmed and the charge is less than 180 days old. Duplicate charges are always refundable. Credits are preferred over cash refunds for amounts under $50.
Refunds up to $5,000 may be approved by a support lead. Any refund above $5,000 requires finance sign-off. Never issue a refund without an approved case in the approval queue.
Standard plans carry a 99.9% monthly uptime commitment. Breaches qualify the customer for service credits equal to 10% of the monthly fee per incident, capped at 50% of one month's fee.
On a confirmed SLA breach, open a remediation case with the vendor within one business day. Do not promise credits beyond the schedule in the uptime commitment section without manager approval.

On suspected exposure of personal data such as SSNs, credit card numbers, or passwords, disable the affected account immediately and notify the privacy lead within one hour. Do not email customer records to anyone.

Customers affected by a confirmed breach must be notified within 72 hours with a plain-language description of what was exposed and what is being done. Legal must review the message before it is sent.

Any report of injury or physical harm connected to our service is a safety incident. Escalate to the senior on-call immediately, document the facts as reported, and never speculate about fault in writing.
Safety incidents require a written follow-up to the reporter within 24 hours. Compensation offers require executive approval.

Treat any report mentioning fraud, scams, phishing, or unauthorized charges as a potential fraud case. Freeze related transactions and escalate to the fraud team before communicating with the customer.
Never ask a customer to send passwords, full card numbers, or SSNs by email or chat. Direct them to the secure portal for any identity verification.
Acknowledge new exceptions within 4 business hours. Low-risk exceptions are summarized and filed; medium and high-risk exceptions require a named owner and a written incident summary.
All customer-facing messages must be drafted, reviewed, and approved before sending. The copilot drafts; a human approves. Automated sending without approval is prohibited.
Low risk: handled by support staff. Medium risk: a support lead owns the case and approves next steps. High risk: the senior on-call is paged and every external action requires explicit approval.
Every escalation includes the incident summary, the risk classification, and the policy sections relied on. Never escalate without the written summary.
Collect and store only the personal data needed for the case. Redact SSNs, full card numbers, and passwords from incident summaries wherever the original report is already quoted.
Incident summaries are retained for 2 years. Raw reporter messages quoted in summaries inherit the same retention schedule.
